archetype.name: Lost Season (defense still intact)
archetype.definition: A team coming off two 11-win years whose defense still plays at a playoff level, while an offense that cannot protect, run or pass has sunk the season before November.

report.headline: A good defense chained to the league's worst, most sack-prone offense
report.take:
These Chargers carried a clear identity into 2026. They won 11 games in each of the last two seasons on the back of defense: the fewest points allowed in the league in 2024, a sixth-ranked defensive EPA last year. The offense was already the weak half in 2025, 23rd in EPA. That half has now collapsed. They are last in offensive EPA, last in passing EPA, last in success rate and scoring 14.1 points a game. The defense is still roughly what it was, 11th in EPA allowed. The 0-7 record is almost entirely an offensive story.

The root of it is up front. The line is 31st in pressure rate allowed, 31st in sack rate and dead last in QB hit rate, and it also leads the league in line penalties at 5.3 a game. The staff's answer has been to hide Justin Herbert. Their pass rate over expected of -11.1 is the most run-heavy in football. But the run game is 30th in run EPA with a bottom-third stuff rate, so leaning on it buys nothing. Herbert's passing EPA has gotten worse in every game since Week 2 and bottomed out at -16.2 against the Rams. That is not a quarterback finding his footing. It is an offense being taken apart a little more each week. The 17 turnovers come with that territory.

The points-allowed number flatters nobody, but it misleads. A unit that ranks 8th against the pass, 6th on third down and 5th in QB hit rate is not a 25-points-a-game defense on its own merits. It keeps defending short fields and long afternoons after giveaways. There is bad luck in the record too: the worst wins-over-expected in the league and no wins in several one-score games, with a differential that implies 2.6 wins. Even so, a 30th-ranked net EPA says this is a bad team, not an unlucky good one. The defense has a real crack as well: 25th in EPA allowed on deep throws. And it just lost Derwin James to IR along with three corners.

The schedule offers some chances: Miami's 31st-ranked defense, a 2-6 Jets team, Houston at home. A few wins are coming. But San Francisco, Kansas City and Denver are still ahead, and nothing in the dossier suggests the protection problem is being solved. Starting guard Kayode Awosika is out this week. Expect the defense to keep games watchable and the offense to keep losing them.

strengths.title: Pass defense that wins third down
strengths.body: The coverage-and-rush combination is still sound. They allow little EPA through the air, get the quarterback on the ground at a top-five rate and get off the field on third down as well as almost anyone. This is the carryover from the 2024-25 defenses, so it is real. The risk is health: James and several corners are out, and that depth is about to be tested.

strengths.title: Still generating takeaways
strengths.body: Ten takeaways ranks 8th, including a five-takeaway game in Buffalo. The defense is doing its part to swing field position. The offense keeps handing the ball straight back. Takeaway rates are streaky, so treat this as a modest, not bankable, edge.

strengths.title: Sound tackling, stingy red zone
strengths.body: They miss few tackles and hold opponents to touchdowns on under half of red-zone trips. That is why the scores stay respectable despite the field position the offense gives away. Disciplined fundamentals like these tend to hold up across a season.

concerns.title: The offensive line is failing everywhere
concerns.body: Pressure, sacks, hits and penalties all land at or near the bottom of the league. That kills drives before the quarterback or play design can matter. It has been true all year, it shows up in both phases, and a starting guard is out this week. No quick fix is in sight.

concerns.title: No lane works: run or pass
concerns.body: They run more than any team relative to expectation, yet the run game is 30th in EPA. Meanwhile the passing game keeps deteriorating, with its worst game coming coming out of the bye. A run-heavy shell built to protect Herbert is producing neither safety nor yards. It's a structural problem, not variance.

concerns.title: Turnovers inflate the points allowed
concerns.body: Seventeen giveaways in seven games is a direct line to the 25 points a game allowed. The defense keeps working on short fields. Some of it is pressure-driven and will persist. Some is fumble-and-bounce noise that should ease, but not enough to flip the record.

trend.note: Passing EPA has sunk in every game since Week 2. The last two games produced 6 and 9 points, including the post-bye loss to the Rams, so the offense is getting worse, not stabilizing.

nextGame.headline: Houston's pass rush meets the league's leakiest protection, indoors
nextGame.body:
Houston comes in 2-5, but it is a much better team than that: nearly even on point differential and nearly as unlucky as the Chargers by wins over expected. The Book has the Texans -4.5 on the road with a 40.5 total, the Chargers +164. The matchup that decides it sits on the Chargers' offensive line. Houston is second in sacks and fifth in sack rate. The Chargers allow sacks at the second-highest rate in the league. Houston's defense does have soft spots: it is near the bottom against the run and gives up explosive passes at the worst rate in football. On the other side, C.J. Stroud runs a 12th-ranked passing offense with a run game that doesn't scare anyone.

The Chargers are thin. Derwin James is on IR. Guard Kayode Awosika and corners Donte Jackson, Deane Leonard and Rodney Shelley are all out. That leaves a secondary short on bodies against a Texans offense that throws well. David Njoku's practice window may open, and Denzel Perryman is close to returning from IR. Houston has its own back-end issues: both starting safeties, Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship, are questionable. David Montgomery is questionable, and receiver Jaylin Noel is out for the season.

waysToWin.title: Make Houston throw on obvious downs
waysToWin.body: Houston's run game is bottom-eight by EPA, so the Chargers can sell out against the pass on early downs. Their third-down defense ranks among the league's best. If Stroud is facing third-and-long all day, the Chargers' pass defense is good enough to keep this a low-scoring game.

waysToWin.title: Run at a soft run defense
waysToWin.body: The Chargers' run-heavy plan has failed against most fronts, but Houston is 29th in rush EPA allowed. That gives the scheme its best shot yet to stay on schedule and keep the pass rush out of the game. Houston also gives up touchdowns on a high share of red-zone trips, so drives that get there can finish.

waysToWin.title: Hit shots on a shaky back end
waysToWin.body: Houston allows explosive passes at the league's worst rate and struggles on deep balls. Opposing second receivers have feasted. With both safeties questionable, a couple of protected deep shots to Tre Harris or Quentin Johnston could carry an offense that otherwise cannot string plays together.

waysToLose.title: The pass rush wrecks every drive
waysToLose.body: Houston gets home as often as nearly any defense, and the Chargers' line has given up four or more sacks in several games. Without Awosika, sacks and drive-killing negative plays are the most likely script. That's how a 15-point offense becomes a 10-point offense.

waysToLose.title: Stroud stretches a depleted secondary
waysToLose.body: The Chargers were already 25th against deep passes before losing James and three corners. Houston's passing offense is efficient enough to find whoever is filling in. A couple of chunk completions would undo an otherwise solid defensive day.

waysToLose.title: Gifts to a defense that rarely takes
waysToLose.body: Houston has forced only six takeaways, so the Chargers should be able to protect the ball. But they have turned it over at a heavy clip and commit the second-most penalties in the league. Extra possessions and short fields are how a close game slips away.

nextGame.watch: First- and second-down pass protection without Awosika. If Herbert is sacked or hit early in drives, Houston's pass rush takes over and nothing else in this game matters.

restOfSeason.body:
Some of this will even out. The differential says this team should have a couple of wins, and turnover luck rarely stays this one-sided, so a few close games should break their way. Miami, the Jets and Houston are the likeliest spots. The defense is the sustainable part, although the James injury and the corner shortage will dent it until bodies return, with James's estimate late November.

What won't regress is the offense's structure. A bottom-two line, a run game that fails even with heavy volume, and a passing game trending down add up to an offense likely to stay in the bottom five. A path out exists if protection firms up with healthy bodies and Njoku's return, but nothing in the dossier points that way yet. With San Francisco, Kansas City and Denver on the back end, a top-five draft slot is far likelier than a respectable finish.
swingFactors: Secondary health: James and the corners

confidence.note: Seven games, but the offensive signal is consistent and worsening; injuries cloud the defense.
